headline.caveat: All-stock acquisition of Anysphere (Cursor) agreed June 2026 — the largest VC-backed startup acquisition ever. Consideration is merged xAI/SpaceX stock; close expected Q3 2026.

realized_to_date.caveat: Not closed; all-stock, so no cash moves even at close — Anysphere holders receive xAI equity.

nature_md: xAI (the merged xAI/SpaceX entity) agreed in June 2026 to acquire Anysphere, maker of the Cursor AI coding tool, for $60B in stock — the largest acquisition of a venture-backed startup on record. Strategic logic: Cursor's developer distribution and usage data plugged into xAI's Grok models and Colossus compute, and coding is the deepest-monetizing AI application category. All-stock consideration leans on xAI's private $1.25T combined valuation mark; close expected Q3 2026, pending customary approvals.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: At close, xAI issues equity — no cash outflow; Anysphere lands on the balance sheet mostly as goodwill/intangibles against a $60B mark set in xAI's own private-valuation currency. Dilution to existing xAI/SpaceX holders is the real cost.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Anysphere shareholders (VCs, employees) swap Cursor equity for xAI stock — no liquidity until an xAI IPO/secondary; the 'price' is only as real as the acquirer's private mark. Cursor's ARR (multi-hundred-$M scale) becomes xAI segment revenue post-close.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** consolidates the fastest-growing AI coding franchise into the Musk compute/model stack, paid in appreciated paper. **Bear:** a $60B all-stock price against private marks on both sides is unfalsifiable value transfer — headline records get set at cycle tops, and the deal has not closed (see Disney-OpenAI withdrawal for how announced ≠ done).

events.title: xAI agrees to acquire Anysphere (Cursor) for $60B in stock

sources.notes: Close expected Q3 2026; terms per announcement — not yet consummated.
